- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.

# Summary of Political Manifesto 2024

## Core Vision
This manifesto presents a plan for addressing interconnected crises: cost of living pressures, climate change, and declining public services. It argues that solutions to environmental challenges simultaneously address social and economic inequalities.

## Healthcare
The document proposes significant NHS investment (£28bn annually by 2030, plus £20bn capital spending over five years) to reduce waiting lists, guarantee GP access, restore NHS dentistry (£3bn annually by 2030), boost staff pay, and reverse privatisation. Mental health services would receive equal priority with physical health, including school counsellors and faster access to therapies.

## Social Care
A £20bn annual investment would fund free personal care modelled on existing Scottish provisions, alongside improved pay and career structures for care workers. Disability benefits would increase by 5%, and children's social care would receive £3bn additional funding.

## Housing
The manifesto proposes 150,000 new social homes annually, ending certain property sale schemes, introducing rent controls, ending no-fault evictions, and a major retrofitting programme (£29bn over five years for home insulation, £9bn for heating systems).

## Energy and Climate
Plans include achieving 70% wind-powered electricity by 2030, ending new fossil fuel extraction, introducing a carbon tax (starting at £120/tonne), and community ownership of energy infrastructure. Nuclear power would be phased out. A "just transition" would support workers moving from carbon-intensive industries.

## Economy
An average £40bn annual green investment programme is proposed, including nationalising railways, water companies, and major energy retailers. Wealth taxes would target assets above £10m (1%) and £1bn (2%). Capital gains and investment income would be taxed equivalently to employment income.

## Employment
Proposals include a £15/hour minimum wage regardless of age, maximum 10:1 pay ratios in organisations, movement toward a four-day working week, restoration of union rights, and equal protections for gig economy workers.

## Welfare
Universal Credit would increase by £40/week, the two-child benefit cap would be abolished, carers' allowance would rise 10%, and the five-week benefit waiting period would end. Long-term goals include Universal Basic Income.

## Environment
A Rights of Nature Act would grant legal personhood to nature, with 30% of land and sea protected by 2030. Water companies would be nationalised, pesticide regulations tightened, and new right-to-roam legislation introduced.

## Education
Proposals include £8bn school investment, abolishing inspection frameworks, ending academy status, removing tax advantages from private education, scrapping university tuition fees, and restoring maintenance grants.

## Transport
The manifesto proposes £10bn annual public transport subsidies, railway nationalisation, local bus control, £2.5bn annual cycling/walking investment, ending petrol/diesel vehicle sales by 2027, and frequent-flyer levies rather than airport expansion.

## Democracy
Reforms would include proportional representation, votes at 16, an elected second chamber replacing the current appointed one, strengthened devolution, and repeal of recent legislation restricting protest rights.

## Immigration
The document advocates ending hostile environment policies, removing income requirements for family visas, establishing safe asylum routes, permitting asylum seekers to work, and abolishing immigration detention except for public safety.

## Justice
Proposals include ending routine stop-and-search, presumption against custodial sentences under two years, £11bn justice system investment, making misogyny a hate crime, and evidence-based drug law reform including decriminalising personal possession.

## International
The manifesto supports ceasefire in ongoing Middle Eastern conflicts, Palestinian statehood recognition, increasing overseas aid to 1% of national income, rejoining European structures, and nuclear disarmament through signing international prohibition treaties.

## Funding
Revenue would come from wealth and capital gains taxes (£50-70bn annually), carbon taxes (up to £80bn by parliament's end), and business tax reforms (£40bn over five years), alongside borrowing for capital investment.
